chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulaym al-Farra', from Dawud, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is the muezzin and imam of the mosque in the city. If on Friday he prays Asr in its time, what should he do with his mosque? He said: 'Pray Asr in its time. When it is that time when the people of the city give the call to prayer, give the call and pray with them in the time that the people of your city pray with them.'

key_terms.الْمِصْرِ: The city (referring to the local community's practice)

ai.seo_question: What should an imam do if he prays Asr early but the congregation prays it later?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical dilemma of a dual-role cleric in a community with distinct prayer timings, emphasizing the importance of maintaining congregational unity (*jamāʿah*) while adhering to individual prayer obligations. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle of accommodating local customs (*ʿurf*) and communal harmony, ensuring the imam does not alienate the people by praying at a different time than the majority.
